classifications.label: Instrumental noise floor dominates; instruments are functioning but measurements are capturing only thermal/electronic jitter unrelated to physical time evolution
Systematic error or miscalibration in one or more instruments; baseline values are offset from true physical quantities but internal reproducibility is high
Environmental or instrumental coupling introduces delayed cross-talk between streams; apparent correlations at specific offsets (e.g., 4–6 day lags) reflect real but indirect interactions
Data collection or logging error; readings are not independent observations of the same phenomenon
Instrumental noise floor dominates; each instrument operates stably but measures uncorrelated noise rather than a shared physical signal
A transient environmental or instrumental perturbation occurred between day 10 and day 20, affecting resonator_obs (and possibly resonator_lab) but leaving pendulum streams relatively stable
Systematic miscalibration or offset in one or more instruments; each measures a different but stable physical quantity, or the same quantity with different baselines

Environmental or instrumental coupling with delayed cross-talk; apparent offset-dependent correlations reflect real but indirect interactions (e.g., thermal diffusion, vibration coupling, stress redistribution)
Data collection or logging error; readings are corrupted, duplicated, or time-tagged incorrectly, but the error structure mimics noise

Resonator_obs apparatus experienced a sudden physical perturbation on day 30 (thermal spike, mechanical shock, electromagnetic interference) that increased measurement scatter and shifted readings upward transiently
Resonator_obs operates near its noise floor, and day-30 readings represent a random high-variance cluster within the expected noise envelope — no real physical change, just statistical fluctuation

Systematic miscalibration or baseline drift in resonator_obs that accumulated over days 11–30 and manifested most visibly on day 30, or a drift in room conditions (temperature, pressure) that resonator_obs tracks but other streams do not

Data logging or time-tag error specific to day 30 for resonator_obs: readings were collected on an earlier or later day but mis-stamped as day 30, or data were acquired in a different order and recorded out of sequence
Measurement streams track genuinely independent physical processes, and observed correlations are statistical noise at or near chance level; no systematic coupling exists.

Environmental conditions (room temperature, humidity, vibration) couple weakly and with different time constants to the four instruments, producing lagged correlations and subtle anti-correlations; a shared common cause produces the lagged structure.

Cross-instrument electromagnetic coupling or ground-loop interference creates weak, frequency-dependent crosstalk at specific phase delays; resonator_obs is most susceptible due to higher Q or different grounding.

Data post-processing or baseline-subtraction error: raw readings are actually well-correlated, but analysis drift (e.g., incorrect reference frame, drifting ADC offset, or baseline miscalibration on day 1) has decorrelated them or introduced spurious anti-correlation.

All observed correlations (positive and negative) are statistical artifacts of multiple-comparison bias; after correction for multiple hypothesis tests (4 streams, 20+ possible time offsets per pair), no significant structure remains.
